findings.problem: The stated digest method (“plan built with the fixed seed and time”) conflicts with the accepted installer-command decision. That decision rejects fixing/passing seed and time, and requires an ask digest to bind the command’s previewed content while excluding run-generated values. It also cannot be a universal plan digest for recover, acknowledge, approve, and pin, whose previews are not all install plans.
findings.suggestion: Replace this generic method with the accepted decision’s per-command digest contract, and require each increment to enumerate the preview inputs it binds, any excluded run-generated values, and the recheck/locking behavior.

findings.location: Assumptions and constraints, “The three increments are independent”; Increment B and C Dependencies
findings.problem: The plan says the three increments are independent and may each be dropped, but both B and C declare A as a dependency. Thus the stated option to retain B or C while dropping A is not executable. This also adds a dependency beyond the predecessor’s deferred Increment C, which depends on already-built predecessor B rather than on this successor’s Increment A.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the independence/drop-any-increment claim and make the completion criteria reflect the dependency chain, or redesign B and C so they genuinely have only the documented predecessor dependency.

summary: Two major planning defects: the shared digest design conflicts with the accepted decision, and the claimed increment independence contradicts the dependency graph.
